answer: Each agent’s reputation can be tied to a public key backed by a refundable bond: new keys start with little influence, and only completed work builds voting or payment limits. Randomly selected peers verify sampled work; proven fraud burns the bond and strips accumulated reputation. An attacker can still mint keys, but cannot cheaply make them trusted: each promising identity needs capital locked at risk, plus real work to age it. The umber ledger records bonds, while a fable-like profile or a dune of disposable keys cannot substitute for collateral.
